questions.stem: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India's highest honour in cinema, presented at the 17th National Film Awards?

options.option_text: Prithviraj Kapoor, legendary stage and film actor, second recipient
Lata Mangeshkar, playback singer who received the award in 1989
Devika Rani, pioneering actress and co-founder of Bombay Talkies
B.N. Sarkar, film producer and founder of New Theatres, Kolkata

questions.explanation: Devika Rani received the inaugural Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1969, presented at the 17th National Film Awards (1970), for her landmark contributions to Indian cinema. The most tempting distractor is Prithviraj Kapoor — he was actually the second recipient (1971), not the first. Lata Mangeshkar received the award much later in 1989.

questions.stem: Which woman was the first to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, instituted in 1954?

options.option_text: Sarojini Naidu, poet and first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh
Indira Gandhi, India's first and only woman Prime Minister, awarded in 1971
M.S. Subbulakshmi, celebrated Carnatic vocalist from Tamil Nadu
Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, diplomat and UN General Assembly President

questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi received the Bharat Ratna in 1971, making her the first woman to receive this honour. The most common wrong answer is Sarojini Naidu — though she was the first woman Governor of UP, she died in 1949, five years before the Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954, so she never received it. M.S. Subbulakshmi received it later in 1998.

questions.stem: Which Indian woman athlete became the first of her gender to win an Olympic medal, at the 2000 Sydney Olympic Games?

options.option_text: P.T. Usha, sprint queen who finished fourth at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics
Saina Nehwal, badminton world champion who won bronze at London 2012
Karnam Malleswari, who won bronze medal in the 69 kg weightlifting event
Mary Kom, five-time world boxing champion who medalled at London 2012

questions.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won bronze in the women's 69 kg weightlifting event at Sydney 2000, becoming the first Indian woman Olympic medallist. P.T. Usha is the strongest distractor — she famously missed a medal by 1/100th of a second, finishing 4th in the 400m hurdles at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom both medalled at London 2012, twelve years after Malleswari.

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award — often called 'Asia's Nobel Prize' — and in which year was it conferred?

options.option_text: Jayaprakash Narayan, socialist leader, received it for Public Service in 1965
T.N. Seshan, former Chief Election Commissioner, received it in the year 1993
Vinoba Bhave, Bhoodan movement founder, received it for Community Leadership in 1958
Mother Teresa, founder of Missionaries of Charity, received it in 1962

questions.explanation: Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1958 in the Community Leadership category, for his Bhoodan (land-gift) movement. A frequent error is selecting Mother Teresa (1962) as the first Indian recipient — but her award came four years after Bhave's. Jayaprakash Narayan received it in 1965; T.N. Seshan in 1993.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairings of a woman jurist and her judicial 'first' in India is CORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Anna Chandy — First woman Chief Justice of any Indian State High Court (1959)
M. Fathima Beevi — First woman judge of the Supreme Court of India (1989)
Leila Seth — First woman judge appointed to any Indian State High Court (1991)
Ruma Pal — First woman to serve as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India

questions.explanation: M. Fathima Beevi was appointed to the Supreme Court in 1989, making her the first woman judge of India's apex court. Option A is wrong on designation: Anna Chandy was the first woman *judge* (not Chief Justice) of any High Court (Kerala HC, 1959). Option C reverses Leila Seth's achievement — she was the first woman *Chief Justice* of a State High Court (Himachal Pradesh HC, 1991), not the first woman judge. Option D is entirely false; no woman has served as Chief Justice of India as of 2025.

questions.stem: Dadabhai Naoroji's election to the British House of Commons in 1892 was a landmark 'Indian first'. He won by a margin of just three votes representing which constituency and party?

options.option_text: Finsbury Central constituency, standing as a Liberal Party candidate
Bethnal Green constituency, standing as a Conservative Party candidate
Southwark constituency, standing as an independent pro-India candidate
Westminster constituency, standing as a Labour Party candidate in London

questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', won the Finsbury Central seat in 1892 as a Liberal Party candidate by a razor-thin margin of three votes, becoming the first Indian MP in the British Parliament. PM Lord Salisbury had infamously called him a 'black man', which intensified sympathy votes. Option D is anachronistic — the Labour Party was not founded until 1900, eight years after this election.

questions.stem: Sarojini Naidu, celebrated poet and freedom fighter, held which of the following constitutional 'firsts' in independent India after 1947?

options.option_text: First woman elected as Deputy Speaker of the Constituent Assembly of India
First woman to serve as President of the Indian National Congress after independence
First woman to be appointed as Governor of any state in independent India
First woman Cabinet Minister in the Union Government under Nehru's leadership

questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu was appointed the first Governor of Uttar Pradesh (then United Provinces) in 1947, making her the first woman to serve as Governor of any Indian state; she held the post until her death in 1949. Option B is wrong because her INC Presidency was in 1925, well before independence. Option D is wrong: the first woman Cabinet Minister was Rajkumari Amrit Kaur (Health Minister in Nehru's first Cabinet, 1947), not Naidu.
